title: Japanese Charts: Castlevania And Tales Of Eternia Battle It Out For The Gold
summary:
Tales of Castlevania.

We are back with our latest look at the Japanese physical charts from Famitsu, and two new releases have been racing for the top spot this week.

Both Tales of Eternia Remastered and Castlevania: Belmont's Curse came out of the gate swinging, but it was the former that just about secured the win, taking 17,911 sales over Castlevania's 15,630.

title: Pokémon Apps Are Coming Back Online After Extended Cybersecurity Outage
summary:
Sleep, HOME and Champions all went down yesterday.

You may have read yesterday about the cybersecurity alert that hit sites and apps around the world after two vulnerabilities were found in the popular programming language, PHP. The Pokémon Company were one of the many teams hit by the outage, with Pokémon HOME, Sleep and Champions all going offline yesterday without an end time in sight. Well, fortunately, they have started to come back.

As shared on the apps' official social media accounts, it seems that TPC is now on top of the issue and is in the process of restoring functionality. Champions was the first to come back online at around 3am BST this morning, followed by HOME a few hours later. Pokémon Sleep was a little later to join the party, but ended its maintenance around 10am BST.

title: EA Outlines Future Development Plans As It Prepares To Cut Around 400 Jobs
summary:
Sports games remain top priority, unsurprisingly.

Alongside the news Electronic Arts is shutting down BioWare and reports about it axing around 400 jobs across the entire company, EA executives have also revealed future development plans.

According to an internal letter to staff, reviewed by Bloomberg, EA says it will continue investing in sports games (such as EA FC). Development on its online battle royale Apex Legends also remains a top priority, and it's supposedly still committed to its next Star Wars Jedi title as well as a new Marvel game starring Iron Man.

title: Minecraft x Dragon Ball Z - 1.1 Legends Update Adds More Characters, New Story Mode Fights & Custom Tournament
summary:
Just a week out from the Switch 2 release.

Last year, Minecraft got a DLC crossover with the manga and anime series Dragon Ball Z. Now, almost a year later, a special "1.1 Legends Update" has been released.

It comes loaded with new fighters (like Bardock, Teen Gohan, Gotenks, Vegito), new battle areas, and you'll also be able to compete in a new custom tournament for up to eight players. You can also continue the story mode with 4 new fights and unlock alternate versions of the original characters.

title: Nintendo Switch Sports Resort Has Been Updated To Ver. 1.1.0, Here Are The Full Patch Notes
summary:
You and Mii.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort releases tomorrow (22nd October), and Nintendo is making sure that launch day goes smoothly by releasing its very first update.

The ver. 1.1.0 update is now available. As is often the case with these launch-day jobbies, its purpose is mainly to enable all of the online modes so everyone can play some non-local multiplayer right from the jump. That said, the update also introduces a Mii frequency adjuster, where you can choose how often your Miis appear in offline competitive sports.

title: Review: JSAUX 6-In-1 Gaming Dock For Switch 2 - Attractive Enough, But No Replacement For The Real Deal
summary:
Wibble-wobble.

At a glance, JSAUX’s 6-in-1 Dock for the Switch 2 is a compelling piece of kit.

In addition to docking your console for TV mode, it also contains four slots to charge Joy-Con, along with space to charge your Pro Controller. With a foldable design, it makes for a handy travel companion, and the slick display screen is a neat little touch that will no doubt draw a few eyes. There are, however, a few glaring issues that hold it back.

title: A Permanent Pokémon Store Is Finally Coming To London
summary:
The first of "several" outside Asia.

After years of us leaving the pop-up shop at the European International Championships and wondering, "why isn't this a permanent thing?", it seems our wishes have finally been answered.

The Pokémon Company has today announced that a "permanent, physical Pokémon store" is set to open in London. The store (not referred to as a 'Pokémon Center' in TPC's official statement, interestingly) will open by 2029, and will offer "a variety of exclusive merchandise and one-of-a-kind experiences for Trainers of all ages".

title: Award-Winning Indie Horror 'Mouthwashing' Finally Arrives On Switch This Month
summary:
Eye spy.

Creepy space horror Mouthwashing became something of an indie sensation when it launched back in 2024. After racking up over 500,000 Steam sales, publisher Critical Reflex announced that a Switch version was in the works and now (a year on from that announcement), we finally have a release date.

As revealed in yesterday's Xbox Showcase, Mouthwashing will launch on the Switch eShop on 29th October — yep, as in next week. It's already available to pre-order on the North American storefront, in fact, for $12.99. We've noticed that the store lists its release date as 10th October, but we're sure that's just a typo (we've reached out to Critical Reflex just to double-check).
